# Analysis plan: effect of BMI on systolic blood pressure

Two-sample Mendelian randomization with summary statistics. Written before any analysis. All data are simulated.

## Question

What is the causal effect of body mass index (BMI) on systolic blood pressure (SBP), in **mmHg per 1 kg/m² higher BMI**?

## Data

`data/main/exposure_bmi_gwas.tsv` (BMI instruments) and `data/main/outcome_sbp_gwas.tsv` (the same variants looked up
in an SBP GWAS). Column definitions, units and coding are in `data/DATA_DICTIONARY.md`.

## Steps

1. **Read and clean.** Treat the outcome missing-value code as missing. Drop instruments with no usable outcome data.
2. **Harmonise** every variant so that the exposure and outcome effects refer to the same allele (the exposure effect
   allele). Resolve strand differences by complementing alleles. For palindromic variants (A/T or C/G), infer the strand
   from allele frequency when the minor allele frequency is at most 0.42; otherwise drop the variant. Record the
   harmonisation action for every variant.
3. **Units.** Express exposure effects per kg/m² (1 SD of BMI = 4.8 kg/m²).
4. **Estimate.** Primary: inverse-variance weighted (IVW), multiplicative random effects. Sensitivity: MR-Egger
   (report the intercept) and weighted median. Report Cochran's Q for IVW.
5. **Outputs.**
   - `results/harmonisation_log.csv`: one row per variant, with its harmonisation action and whether it was used
   - `results/estimates.csv`: `method, estimate, se, ci_lower, ci_upper, n_snps`
   - `results/figures/scatter.png`: SNP–outcome against SNP–exposure effects, with the fitted lines
   - `report.md`: at most 200 words for the research group

# Data dictionary

> **All data in this folder are SIMULATED** for the IEU AI-for-coding workshop. They describe no real people,
> variants or GWAS. Variant identifiers are synthetic.

## Files

`main/` holds one exposure GWAS file and one outcome GWAS file for the research question.

## `exposure_bmi_gwas.tsv` (exposure: body mass index)

Genetic instruments for BMI from a GWAS of 300,000 people: independent variants (r² < 0.001) associated with BMI at
P < 5×10⁻⁸, pre-selected by the exposure consortium. The exposure consortium does not guarantee which DNA strand
alleles are reported on.

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `SNP` | Variant identifier |
| `CHR`, `POS` | Chromosome and position (GRCh38) |
| `EFFECT_ALLELE` | Allele whose effect is reported |
| `OTHER_ALLELE` | Other allele |
| `EAF` | Frequency of `EFFECT_ALLELE` |
| `BETA` | Per-copy effect of `EFFECT_ALLELE` on BMI, in **standard-deviation units** (1 SD of BMI = 4.8 kg/m²) |
| `SE` | Standard error of `BETA` (same units) |
| `P` | P-value |
| `N` | Sample size |

## `outcome_sbp_gwas.tsv` (outcome: systolic blood pressure)

Look-up of the BMI instruments in a separate GWAS of SBP (750,000 people, no sample overlap with the exposure GWAS).
Alleles are reported on the forward strand of GRCh38. Some instruments were not available in the outcome GWAS.
**Missing values are coded as `-9`.**

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `rsid` | Variant identifier |
| `chr`, `pos` | Chromosome and position (GRCh38) |
| `A1` | Reference allele |
| `A2` | Alternative allele. **`beta` and `freq` refer to `A2`** |
| `freq` | Frequency of `A2` |
| `beta` | Per-copy effect of `A2` on SBP, in mmHg |
| `se` | Standard error of `beta` |
| `pval` | P-value |
| `n` | Sample size |

1	#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
     2	# Two-sample MR: effect of BMI on systolic blood pressure (mmHg per 1 kg/m2).
     3	# Implements analysis_plan.md using base R only.
     4	# Usage (from the project root): Rscript analysis/mr_analysis.R [dataset_folder]
     5	# Default dataset folder: data/main. Outputs go to results/ and report.md in the working directory.
     6	
     7	args <- commandArgs(trailingOnly = TRUE)
     8	data_dir <- if (length(args) >= 1) args[1] else "data/main"
     9	
    10	SD_BMI_KGM2  <- 4.8    # 1 SD of BMI in kg/m2 (data dictionary)
    11	MAF_MAX_PAL  <- 0.42   # palindromic variants with MAF above this are dropped
    12	MISSING_CODE <- -9     # outcome missing-value code
    13	set.seed(20240601)     # for the weighted-median bootstrap
    14	
    15	dir.create("results/figures", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
    16	
    17	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 1. Read and clean
    18	exp_file <- file.path(data_dir, "exposure_bmi_gwas.tsv")
    19	out_file <- file.path(data_dir, "outcome_sbp_gwas.tsv")
    20	stopifnot(file.exists(exp_file), file.exists(out_file))
    21	
    22	exposure <- read.delim(exp_file, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, na.strings = c("NA", ""))
    23	outcome  <- read.delim(out_file, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, na.strings = c("NA", ""))
    24	
    25	# -9 is the outcome's missing code (numeric columns; also guard allele columns)
    26	for (v in c("chr", "pos", "freq", "beta", "se", "pval", "n")) {
    27	  if (v %in% names(outcome)) {
    28	    outcome[[v]] <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(outcome[[v]]))
    29	    outcome[[v]][!is.na(outcome[[v]]) & outcome[[v]] == MISSING_CODE] <- NA
    30	  }
    31	}
    32	for (v in c("A1", "A2")) outcome[[v]][outcome[[v]] %in% as.character(MISSING_CODE)] <- NA
    33	outcome$A1 <- toupper(outcome$A1); outcome$A2 <- toupper(outcome$A2)
    34	exposure$EFFECT_ALLELE <- toupper(exposure$EFFECT_ALLELE)
    35	exposure$OTHER_ALLELE  <- toupper(exposure$OTHER_ALLELE)
    36	
    37	if (anyDuplicated(exposure$SNP)) stop("Duplicate SNP ids in exposure file")
    38	if (anyDuplicated(outcome$rsid)) stop("Duplicate rsid in outcome file")
    39	
    40	dat <- merge(exposure, outcome, by.x = "SNP", by.y = "rsid", all.x = TRUE, sort = FALSE)
    41	dat <- dat[match(exposure$SNP, dat$SNP), ]   # keep exposure order
    42	
    43	in_outcome  <- dat$SNP %in% outcome$rsid
    44	usable_out  <- in_outcome & !is.na(dat$beta) & !is.na(dat$se) & dat$se > 0 &
    45	               !is.na(dat$A1) & !is.na(dat$A2)
    46	
    47	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 2. Harmonise
    48	# Target: outcome effect expressed for the exposure effect allele (EA).
    49	comp <- function(a) c(A = "T", T = "A", C = "G", G = "C")[a]
    50	is_pal <- function(a, b) paste0(sort(c(a, b)), collapse = "") %in% c("AT", "CG")
    51	
    52	dat$action <- NA_character_
    53	dat$flip   <- NA     # TRUE: outcome beta must be negated and freq -> 1 - freq
    54	dat$out_freq_ea <- NA_real_   # outcome frequency of the exposure EA after harmonisation
    55	
    56	for (i in seq_len(nrow(dat))) {
    57	  if (!in_outcome[i]) { dat$action[i] <- "dropped: not in outcome GWAS"; next }
    58	  if (!usable_out[i]) { dat$action[i] <- "dropped: outcome data missing (-9)"; next }
    59	
    60	  ea <- dat$EFFECT_ALLELE[i]; oa <- dat$OTHER_ALLELE[i]
    61	  a1 <- dat$A1[i];            a2 <- dat$A2[i]
    62	  if (!all(c(ea, oa, a1, a2) %in% c("A", "C", "G", "T"))) {
    63	    dat$action[i] <- "dropped: non-ACGT or indel alleles"; next
    64	  }
    65	  # outcome effect is for A2; frequency of EA in outcome if strands agree
    66	  if (is_pal(ea, oa)) {
    67	    if (!(a1 == ea && a2 == oa) && !(a1 == oa && a2 == ea)) {
    68	      dat$action[i] <- "dropped: allele mismatch"; next
    69	    }
    70	    eaf <- dat$EAF[i]
    71	    f_naive <- if (a2 == ea) dat$freq[i] else 1 - dat$freq[i]   # assumes same strand
    72	    if (is.na(eaf) || is.na(f_naive) ||
    73	        min(eaf, 1 - eaf) > MAF_MAX_PAL ||
    74	        min(dat$freq[i], 1 - dat$freq[i]) > MAF_MAX_PAL) {
    75	      dat$action[i] <- "dropped: palindromic, MAF > 0.42 (strand ambiguous)"; next
    76	    }
    77	    same_strand <- (eaf < 0.5) == (f_naive < 0.5)
    78	    if (same_strand) {
    79	      dat$flip[i] <- (a2 != ea)
    80	      dat$out_freq_ea[i] <- f_naive
    81	      dat$action[i] <- if (dat$flip[i]) "palindromic: same strand (inferred from EAF), flipped"
    82	                       else "palindromic: same strand (inferred from EAF), no flip"
    83	    } else {
    84	      # opposite strand: outcome A2 is the complement of the allele it appears to be
    85	      dat$flip[i] <- (a2 == ea)
    86	      dat$out_freq_ea[i] <- 1 - f_naive
    87	      dat$action[i] <- if (dat$flip[i]) "palindromic: strand flipped (inferred from EAF), flipped"
    88	                       else "palindromic: strand flipped (inferred from EAF), no flip"
    89	    }
    90	    next
    91	  }
    92	  # non-palindromic
    93	  if (a2 == ea && a1 == oa) {
    94	    dat$flip[i] <- FALSE; dat$action[i] <- "none: alleles aligned"
    95	  } else if (a2 == oa && a1 == ea) {
    96	    dat$flip[i] <- TRUE;  dat$action[i] <- "flipped: allele order swapped"
    97	  } else if (a2 == comp(ea) && a1 == comp(oa)) {
    98	    dat$flip[i] <- FALSE; dat$action[i] <- "strand: complemented, no flip"
    99	  } else if (a2 == comp(oa) && a1 == comp(ea)) {
   100	    dat$flip[i] <- FALSE; dat$action[i] <- "strand: complemented, no flip"
   101	  } else {
   102	    dat$action[i] <- "dropped: allele mismatch"; next
   103	  }
   104	  dat$out_freq_ea[i] <- if (dat$flip[i]) 1 - dat$freq[i] else dat$freq[i]
   105	}
   106	
   107	dat$used <- !is.na(dat$flip)
   108	dat$beta_out_h <- ifelse(dat$used, ifelse(dat$flip, -dat$beta, dat$beta), NA)
   109	
   110	harm_log <- data.frame(
   111	  SNP = dat$SNP, exposure_EA = dat$EFFECT_ALLELE, exposure_OA = dat$OTHER_ALLELE,
   112	  exposure_EAF = dat$EAF, outcome_A1 = dat$A1, outcome_A2 = dat$A2,
   113	  outcome_freq_A2 = dat$freq, harmonisation_action = dat$action, used = dat$used,
   114	  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
   115	write.csv(harm_log, "results/harmonisation_log.csv", row.names = FALSE)
   116	
   117	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 3. Units
   118	# Exposure effects per kg/m2 (data are per SD); outcome already in mmHg.
   119	mr <- dat[dat$used, ]
   120	bx  <- mr$BETA / SD_BMI_KGM2
   121	sex <- mr$SE   / SD_BMI_KGM2
   122	by  <- mr$beta_out_h
   123	sey <- mr$se
   124	n   <- length(bx)
   125	if (n < 4) stop("Too few usable instruments (", n, ") for MR-Egger")
   126	cat(sprintf("%d of %d variants used\n", n, nrow(dat)))
   127	
   128	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 4. Estimate
   129	z975 <- qnorm(0.975)
   130	
   131	# IVW, multiplicative random effects (residual SE scaled, not allowed below 1)
   132	w <- 1 / sey^2
   133	ivw_fit <- lm(by ~ 0 + bx, weights = w)
   134	ivw_b   <- unname(coef(ivw_fit))
   135	sigma_i <- summary(ivw_fit)$sigma
   136	ivw_se  <- sqrt(1 / sum(w * bx^2)) * max(1, sigma_i)
   137	Q       <- sum(w * (by - ivw_b * bx)^2)
   138	Q_df    <- n - 1
   139	Q_p     <- pchisq(Q, Q_df, lower.tail = FALSE)
   140	I2      <- max(0, (Q - Q_df) / Q)
   141	
   142	# MR-Egger: orient so every SNP-exposure effect is positive
   143	sgn <- sign(bx); sgn[sgn == 0] <- 1
   144	bx_o <- bx * sgn; by_o <- by * sgn
   145	eg_fit  <- lm(by_o ~ bx_o, weights = w)
   146	eg_sum  <- summary(eg_fit)
   147	eg_sig  <- max(1, eg_sum$sigma)
   148	eg_coef <- eg_sum$coefficients
   149	eg_df   <- n - 2
   150	eg_int  <- eg_coef[1, 1]; eg_int_se <- eg_coef[1, 2] / eg_sum$sigma * eg_sig
   151	eg_b    <- eg_coef[2, 1]; eg_b_se   <- eg_coef[2, 2] / eg_sum$sigma * eg_sig
   152	tcrit   <- qt(0.975, eg_df)
   153	
   154	# Weighted median (Bowden 2016), first-order weights, parametric bootstrap SE
   155	wmedian <- function(b, wt) {
   156	  o <- order(b); b <- b[o]; wt <- wt[o] / sum(wt)
   157	  p <- cumsum(wt) - 0.5 * wt
   158	  below <- max(which(p < 0.5))
   159	  b[below] + (b[below + 1] - b[below]) * (0.5 - p[below]) / (p[below + 1] - p[below])
   160	}
   161	ratio    <- by / bx
   162	se_ratio <- sey / abs(bx)
   163	wm_b <- wmedian(ratio, 1 / se_ratio^2)
   164	boot <- replicate(1000, {
   165	  bxs <- rnorm(n, bx, sex); bys <- rnorm(n, by, sey)
   166	  wmedian(bys / bxs, 1 / (sey / abs(bxs))^2)
   167	})
   168	wm_se <- sd(boot)
   169	
   170	estimates <- data.frame(
   171	  method   = c("IVW (multiplicative random effects)", "MR-Egger", "MR-Egger intercept", "Weighted median"),
   172	  estimate = c(ivw_b, eg_b, eg_int, wm_b),
   173	  se       = c(ivw_se, eg_b_se, eg_int_se, wm_se),
   174	  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
   175	crit <- c(z975, tcrit, tcrit, z975)
   176	estimates$ci_lower <- estimates$estimate - crit * estimates$se
   177	estimates$ci_upper <- estimates$estimate + crit * estimates$se
   178	estimates$n_snps   <- n
   179	estimates <- estimates[, c("method", "estimate", "se", "ci_lower", "ci_upper", "n_snps")]
   180	write.csv(estimates, "results/estimates.csv", row.names = FALSE)
   181	
   182	cat(sprintf("IVW Cochran's Q = %.2f (df %d, p = %.3g), I2 = %.2f\n", Q, Q_df, Q_p, I2))
   183	print(estimates, digits = 4)
   184	
   185	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 5. Scatter plot
   186	png("results/figures/scatter.png", width = 1600, height = 1200, res = 200)
   187	xlim <- range(c(0, bx_o - z975 * sex, bx_o + z975 * sex))
   188	ylim <- range(c(by_o - z975 * sey, by_o + z975 * sey, 0))
   189	plot(bx_o, by_o, pch = 16, col = "grey30", xlim = xlim, ylim = ylim,
   190	     xlab = "SNP effect on BMI (kg/m2 per allele)",
   191	     ylab = "SNP effect on SBP (mmHg per allele)",
   192	     main = "BMI -> SBP: SNP-outcome vs SNP-exposure effects")
   193	segments(bx_o, by_o - z975 * sey, bx_o, by_o + z975 * sey, col = "grey70")
   194	segments(bx_o - z975 * sex, by_o, bx_o + z975 * sex, by_o, col = "grey70")
   195	abline(h = 0, v = 0, lty = 3, col = "grey80")
   196	abline(0, ivw_b, col = "firebrick", lwd = 2)
   197	abline(eg_int, eg_b, col = "steelblue", lwd = 2)
   198	abline(0, wm_b, col = "darkgreen", lwd = 2)
   199	legend("topleft", bty = "n", lwd = 2,
   200	       col = c("firebrick", "steelblue", "darkgreen"),
   201	       legend = c("IVW", "MR-Egger", "Weighted median"))
   202	mtext("Effects oriented so SNP-exposure effects are positive; bars are 95% CIs", side = 1, line = 4, cex = 0.7)
   203	dev.off()
   204	
   205	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- report.md (<= 200 words)
   206	n_drop <- nrow(dat) - n
   207	fmt <- function(i) sprintf("%.2f (95%% CI %.2f to %.2f)", estimates$estimate[i], estimates$ci_lower[i], estimates$ci_upper[i])
   208	report <- c(
   209	  "# BMI and systolic blood pressure: Mendelian randomization (simulated data)",
   210	  "",
   211	  sprintf("**Question.** Causal effect of BMI on SBP, in mmHg per 1 kg/m2 higher BMI.", ""),
   212	  "",
   213	  sprintf("**Data.** %d BMI instruments; %d used after harmonisation (%d dropped for missing outcome data, allele mismatch or ambiguous palindromic strand; see `results/harmonisation_log.csv`).", nrow(dat), n, n_drop),
   214	  "",
   215	  sprintf("**Results.** IVW (random effects): %s mmHg per kg/m2. Weighted median: %s. MR-Egger: %s.", fmt(1), fmt(4), fmt(2)),
   216	  "",
   217	  sprintf("**Heterogeneity and pleiotropy.** Cochran's Q = %.1f on %d df (p = %.2g). MR-Egger intercept = %.3f mmHg (95%% CI %.3f to %.3f).", Q, Q_df, Q_p, eg_int, estimates$ci_lower[3], estimates$ci_upper[3]),
   218	  "",
   219	  "**Caveats.** Results rest on the usual MR assumptions, which these checks cannot prove. Data are simulated; do not interpret as real findings."
   220	)
   221	words <- length(strsplit(paste(report, collapse = " "), "\\s+")[[1]])
   222	if (words > 200) warning("report.md has ", words, " words (limit 200)")
   223	writeLines(report, "report.md")
   224	cat("Done. Report words:", words, "\n")

# BMI and systolic blood pressure: Mendelian randomization (simulated data)

**Question.** Causal effect of BMI on SBP, in mmHg per 1 kg/m2 higher BMI.

**Data.** 100 BMI instruments; 89 used. Dropped: 4 absent from the outcome GWAS, 3 with missing outcome data, 4 ambiguous palindromic variants (MAF > 0.42). Details: `results/harmonisation_log.csv`.

**Results (mmHg per kg/m2).**
- IVW (random effects): 1.59 (95% CI -0.03 to 3.21)
- Weighted median: 3.29 (95% CI 1.00 to 5.58)
- MR-Egger: 5.42 (95% CI 0.61 to 10.22)

All estimates are positive, but IVW is imprecise and its interval includes zero. The methods differ considerably, so the size of the effect is uncertain.

**Heterogeneity and pleiotropy.** Cochran's Q = 135.6 on 88 df (p = 0.00084): clear heterogeneity. MR-Egger intercept = -0.024 mmHg (95% CI -0.052 to 0.004): no clear directional pleiotropy, though the interval is wide.

**Caveats.** Results rest on MR assumptions these checks cannot prove. Data are simulated; do not interpret as real findings.

**Question.** Causal effect of BMI on SBP, in mmHg per 1 kg/m2 higher BMI.

**Data.** 100 BMI instruments; 89 used. Dropped: 4 absent from the outcome GWAS, 3 with missing outcome data, 4 ambiguous palindromic variants (MAF > 0.42). Details: `results/harmonisation_log.csv`.

- IVW (random effects): 1.59 (95% CI -0.03 to 3.21)
- Weighted median: 3.29 (95% CI 1.00 to 5.58)
- MR-Egger: 5.42 (95% CI 0.61 to 10.22)

All estimates are positive, but IVW is imprecise and its interval includes zero. The methods differ considerably, so the size of the effect is uncertain.

**Caveats.** Results rest on MR assumptions these checks cannot prove. Data are simulated; do not interpret as real findings.

# Independent check of the script's flip decision using allele frequency.
# For non-palindromic variants (MAF away from 0.5) the outcome frequency of the exposure
# effect allele, implied by the script's flip decision, should be close to exposure EAF.
args <- commandArgs(trailingOnly = TRUE)
W <- args[1]
lg <- read.csv(file.path(W, "results/harmonisation_log.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
comp <- function(a) c(A = "T", T = "A", C = "G", G = "C")[a]
u <- lg[lg$used & !grepl("^palindromic", lg$harmonisation_action), ]
# what the script did: flip TRUE only for "flipped: allele order swapped"
script_flip <- u$harmonisation_action == "flipped: allele order swapped"
# independent truth from alleles: is outcome A2 (after strand-alignment) the exposure EA?
a2_on_exp_strand <- ifelse(u$harmonisation_action == "none: alleles aligned" |
                           u$harmonisation_action == "flipped: allele order swapped",
                           u$outcome_A2,
                           ifelse(u$outcome_A2 %in% c("A","C","G","T"), comp(u$outcome_A2), NA))
true_flip <- a2_on_exp_strand != u$exposure_EA
freq_ea_script <- ifelse(script_flip, 1 - u$outcome_freq_A2, u$outcome_freq_A2)
freq_ea_true   <- ifelse(true_flip,   1 - u$outcome_freq_A2, u$outcome_freq_A2)
u$d_script <- abs(freq_ea_script - u$exposure_EAF)
u$d_true   <- abs(freq_ea_true   - u$exposure_EAF)
u$script_flip <- script_flip; u$true_flip <- true_flip
cat("Variants where script flip != allele-derived flip:", sum(script_flip != true_flip), "of", nrow(u), "\n")
cat("Of those, by action:\n"); print(table(u$harmonisation_action[script_flip != true_flip]))
bad <- u$d_script > 0.2
cat("Frequency-implied mismatch (|EAF - outcome freq of EA| > 0.2) under script's flip:", sum(bad), "\n")
cat("Same, under allele-derived flip:", sum(u$d_true > 0.2), "\n")
cat("Rows with freq mismatch under script flip == rows where script_flip != true_flip? ",
    all(bad[u$d_script > 0.2] == (script_flip != true_flip)[u$d_script > 0.2]), "\n")
cat("Max |diff| under allele-derived flip (excl. mismatch rows):", max(u$d_true), "\n")
write.csv(u[script_flip != true_flip, ], file.path("review", "wrong_sign_variants.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

add("nonpal_aligned",            30, FALSE, TRUE,  FALSE)
add("nonpal_swapped",            30, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE)
add("nonpal_comp",               30, FALSE, TRUE,  TRUE)    # EA = comp(A2)
add("nonpal_comp_swapped",       30, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE)    # EA = comp(A1)  (EA label == comp of A1)

add("outcome_freq_missing_nonpal",3, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE,  "maf<=.42", "freq_missing")
add("outcome_freq_missing_pal",   2, TRUE,  TRUE,  FALSE, "maf<=.42", "freq_missing")

add("not_in_outcome",             5, FALSE, TRUE,  FALSE, "maf<=.42", "absent")

  g <- sample(c(-1, 1), 1) * runif(1, .025, .07)                              # true effect of V on BMI (SD)
  # outcome (forward strand)

    P = signif(2 * pnorm(-zx), 3), N = 300000, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

  by_V <- TRUE_EFFECT * g / SD_BMI + rnorm(1, 0, SE_Y)
  by_A2 <- if (A2 == V) by_V else -by_V
  fr_A2 <- min(max((if (A2 == V) f else 1 - f) + rnorm(1, 0, .01), .01), .99)
  row <- data.frame(rsid = id, chr = exp_rows[[k]]$CHR, pos = exp_rows[[k]]$POS, A1 = A1, A2 = A2,
    freq = round(fr_A2, 4), beta = round(by_A2, 7), se = round(SE_Y, 7),

  if (s$extra == "beta_missing")   row[c("beta", "se", "pval")] <- -9
  if (s$extra == "freq_missing")   row$freq <- -9
  if (s$extra == "allele_missing") { row$A1 <- "-9"; row$A2 <- "-9" }
  if (s$extra == "mismatch")       { row$A1 <- "A"; row$A2 <- "C"; exp_rows[[k]]$EFFECT_ALLELE <- "A"; exp_rows[[k]]$OTHER_ALLELE <- "G" }

  if (s$extra == "freq_missing" && !s$pal) exp_used <- TRUE
  if (s$extra == "freq_missing" && s$pal)  exp_used <- FALSE
  if (s$extra == "ambig") exp_used <- FALSE
  truth[[k]] <- data.frame(SNP = id, category = s$cat, expected_used = exp_used,
    expected_flip = (ea_fwd != A2),   # outcome beta (for A2) must be negated to refer to the exposure EA
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}
exposure <- do.call(rbind, exp_rows); outcome <- do.call(rbind, out_rows); truth <- do.call(rbind, truth)
exposure <- exposure[sample(nrow(exposure)), ]; outcome <- outcome[sample(nrow(outcome)), ]
write.table(exposure, file.path(outdir, "exposure_bmi_gwas.tsv"), sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
write.table(outcome,  file.path(outdir, "outcome_sbp_gwas.tsv"),  sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(truth, file.path(outdir, "truth.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
cat("variants:", nrow(exposure), " in outcome:", nrow(outcome), " expected used:", sum(truth$expected_used), "\n")
print(table(truth$category, truth$expected_used))

**Data.** 100 BMI instruments; 89 used after harmonisation (11 dropped for missing outcome data, allele mismatch or ambiguous palindromic strand; see `results/harmonisation_log.csv`).

**Don't share this analysis yet.** The script mishandles one allele situation, and that changes the headline result. The reported IVW estimate is 1.59 (95% CI −0.03 to 3.21). With the bug fixed it is 4.77 (3.45 to 6.09). The Q-statistic conclusion reverses too.

I did not edit `analysis/`, `results/` or `report.md`; their hashes match the ones I took before starting. Everything I produced is in `review/`.

## The bug

`analysis/mr_analysis.R:99-100`: when the outcome's `A2` is the complement of the exposure's *other* allele, the outcome beta belongs to the opposite allele, so it should be negated. The code sets `flip <- FALSE` and labels it "strand: complemented, no flip".

- **Extent:** 27 of the 44 "complemented" variants in the real log have `A2 = comp(OA)`. That is 27 of 89 used variants (30%) with the wrong sign.
- **Independent check:** I compared the outcome frequency of the exposure effect allele with `EAF` (`review/freq_check.R`). Under the script's flips, 16 variants disagree grossly. Under the allele-derived flips, all 85 non-palindromic variants agree to within 0.026. The other 11 sit near MAF 0.5, where frequency can't discriminate.

## 1. Plan against code

| Plan step | Code | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Treat `-9` as missing, drop unusable | lines 26-32, 44-45, 57-58 | Matches. The log counts are 4 not in outcome and 3 with missing data. |
| 2. Harmonise, complement strands | lines 93-103 | **Does not match.** The sign is wrong for `A2 = comp(OA)` (the bug above). |
| 2. Palindromic: MAF ≤ 0.42, infer strand from allele frequency | lines 11, 66-90 | Matches. It also applies the cutoff to the outcome frequency, which is slightly stricter than the plan. |
| 2. Log every variant | lines 110-115 | Matches: 100 rows. The log has no flip column, and its label "no flip" is wrong for 27 rows. |
| 3. Units: per kg/m² | lines 120-121, `BETA / 4.8` | Matches the dictionary. BETA is per SD and 1 SD = 4.8 kg/m², so dividing gives per kg/m². The simulation recovers the truth to 0.5 SE, which confirms the units. |
| 4. IVW (multiplicative random effects), Egger with intercept, weighted median, Q | lines 132-168 | Matches the plan, including the Egger orientation. Both are exact in the patched simulation. |
| 5. Outputs, report ≤ 200 words | `results/*`, `report.md` | The files exist and `report.md` has 160 words. The scatter plot is drawn from the wrongly signed data. |

I reran the script as shipped (`review/repro`). It reproduces `estimates.csv` and the log exactly.

## 2. Known-answer simulation

`review/simulate.R` builds 194 variants with a true effect of **2.0 mmHg per kg/m²** and every allele situation:

- aligned, swapped, complemented, and complemented-and-swapped
- palindromic on the same strand and on the opposite strand, each with `EA = A2` and `EA = A1`
- ambiguous palindromic (MAF above 0.42)
- `-9` in beta, in the frequency (non-palindromic and palindromic) and in the alleles
- an allele mismatch
- variants absent from the outcome

I ran the unchanged script from `review/sim/run_orig`.

- **Kept or dropped:** all 23 drops and 171 keeps are correct.
- **Sign:** 138 of 171 are correct. The 33 failures are all the complemented-and-swapped variants: 30, plus 3 missing-frequency variants built the same way.
- **Estimates:**

| Method | Unchanged script | Patched copy |
|---|---|---|
| IVW | 1.20 (0.95 to 1.45), 6.2 SE below truth | 2.016 (1.95 to 2.08) |
| MR-Egger | 0.77 (−0.18 to 1.73) | 2.011 (1.76 to 2.26) |
| Weighted median | 1.87 | 2.001 |
| Egger intercept | 0.005 | 0.00005 |

The patched copy is `review/mr_analysis_PATCHED_copy.R`. It changes only line 100, to `flip <- TRUE`. The unchanged script **does not** recover the effect.

## 3. Hand check (real data, one variant per action)

I reasoned each expected sign from the alleles and frequencies (`review/hand_check.R`). The script's actual harmonised beta is in the last column.

| Action | Variant | Hand reasoning | Script |
|---|---|---|---|
| none | rs19369461 | EA=G is `A2`, so keep the sign (−) | − ✓ |
| swapped | rs94071924 | `A2` is the other allele, so negate (0.065 becomes −) | − ✓ |
| complemented, `A2 = comp(EA)` | rs62087431 | `A2=G` is the complement of C, so keep (+) | + ✓ |
| **complemented, `A2 = comp(OA)`** | **rs73176882** | EA=C, OA=T, `A2=A=comp(T)`. The beta is for the other allele, so negate: **+0.057**. Frequency agrees: 1 − 0.402 ≈ EAF 0.594. | **−0.057 ✗** |
| palindromic, same strand | rs49900600 | EAF 0.117 and `freq(A2=T)` 0.103, so same strand and keep (−) | − ✓ |
| palindromic, opposite strand, flipped | rs93437852 | EAF 0.147 but `freq(A2=T)` 0.851, so `A2` is the other allele; negate (+0.082 becomes −) | − ✓ |
| palindromic, opposite strand, no flip | rs58559743 | EAF(C) 0.107 and `freq(A2=G)` 0.095, so `A2` is the EA; keep (−) | − ✓ |
| dropped: ambiguous palindromic | rs90247876 | MAF 0.48 > 0.42 | dropped ✓ |
| dropped: `-9` | rs77134306 | beta, se and p are all `-9` | dropped ✓ |
| dropped: absent | rs50795004 | no outcome row | dropped ✓ |

Nine of the ten match. The one exception is the bug.

## 4. Claims in `report.md`

The corrected numbers come from `review/real_patched/`, run from my patched copy.

| Sentence | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Question (units) | **Release** | |
| "100 instruments; 89 used. Dropped: 4 absent, 3 missing, 4 ambiguous palindromic" | **Release** | Log counts are 4, 3 and 4. The patched run also gives 89. |
| IVW 1.59 (−0.03 to 3.21) | **Withdraw, then revise** | Corrected: 4.77 (3.45 to 6.09). |
| Weighted median 3.29 (1.00 to 5.58) | **Withdraw, then revise** | Corrected: 5.20 (3.15 to 7.26). |
| MR-Egger 5.42 (0.61 to 10.22) | **Withdraw, then revise** | Corrected: 7.33 (3.39 to 11.26). |
| "IVW is imprecise and its interval includes zero" | **Withdraw** | The corrected IVW interval excludes zero. |
| "The methods differ considerably, so the size is uncertain" | **Withdraw** | Corrected estimates are 4.8, 5.2 and 7.3, with overlapping intervals. Egger is wide but consistent. |
| "Q = 135.6 on 88 df (p = 0.00084): clear heterogeneity" | **Withdraw** | Corrected: Q = 89.9 on 88 df, p = 0.42. The heterogeneity was produced by the sign errors. |
| "Egger intercept −0.024 (−0.052 to 0.004): no clear directional pleiotropy, though the interval is wide" | **Revise** | Corrected: −0.016 (−0.039 to 0.007). The conclusion holds but the numbers change. |
| Caveats | **Release** | |

`README.md` repeats the wrong headline numbers. `results/figures/scatter.png` and both CSVs also need regenerating.

## What I could not settle

- The corrected figures come from my patched copy. Someone needs to apply the one-line fix in `analysis/` and rerun before the report is rewritten.
- The corrected IVW of 4.77 is about 3.5 SE from 1.59. I trust it because the simulation recovers the truth and the frequency check agrees. I can't say what effect the data's author intended.
- Minor: line 211 gives a harmless `sprintf` warning. The script overwrites the hand-edited `report.md`. `read.delim` would read an allele column that is all "T" as logical. None of these affect the current results.

## Notes on how I worked

- `AGENTS.md` says scratch files go in `scratch/`. I used `review/`, as you asked.
- Three shell calls were auto-denied, for a heredoc, a `cd` combined with a write, and a shell variable. I did not retry them. I redid the same steps with the file-write tool and with literal paths. Nothing was skipped.

Everything is in `review/`. Start with `compare.R` and its outputs under `sim/`, `hand_check.R`, and `real_patched/results/`.
